source.title: PLAYING GTA 6 EARLY ACCESS GAMEPLAY GET IN HERE!
source.duration_note: still live at the time this pack was written (26k concurrent). A 9-10 hour VOD: expect roughly 32000-36000 s once it lands. Do not guess; capture.sh takes any length.
source.timing_note: Stream moments are found by watching, not by transcript. capture.sh takes the seconds you pick and cuts them immediately, which is the whole point: Speed's reactions are a race, the meme dies in about 48 hours.

style.note: Speed yellow on black. Different from the boss pack's GTA red so the two sets never look like one series.

targets.what: The first 30 seconds after he actually gets control of the game
targets.why: The single most-clipped moment of any launch stream. Face cam and game both on screen; keep both.
targets.look_for: his face before the game loads, then the cut to gameplay

targets.what: First wanted level and first bust: the cop chase
targets.why: Cop chases are the most reliable Speed content there is, and GTA 6's heat system makes him argue with the game.
targets.look_for: stars going up, him shouting at the car, the bust animation

targets.what: The first time the car-theft flow does not work the way he expects
targets.why: GTA 6 gates nice cars behind a phone app and security. He is going to find that out loudly.
targets.look_for: the phone out, a locked car, an alarm

targets.what: First look at Vice City / Leonida skyline at night or in a storm
targets.why: Visual payoff clips travel beyond his audience. Hurricane or storm weather is the one to catch.
targets.look_for: rain, lightning, puddles, him going quiet for a second

targets.what: First animal encounter, ideally the alligator
targets.why: 170+ species in this game. A gator biting him is a 15-second clip that needs no context at all.
targets.look_for: swamp, water, a shape in the water

rules.length: 12-40 s. Speed clips live or die on the first 1.5 s, so start ON the shout, not before it.
rules.cut_the_wait: Cut loading screens, menu time and dead air inside a clip; capture.sh takes one continuous range, so pick ranges that have no dead air.
rules.audio: He is loud and peaks. capture.sh normalises to -14 LUFS but if a clip clips, re-cut with a -2 dB trim (documented in README).
rules.credit: Burned into every frame: CLIP: IShowSpeed. Keep @IShowSpeed in the caption too.

capture.note: Fill this in as you pick moments: tools/set_moment.py writes it for you. 60 fps default because the source is a 60 fps stream.
